skill.name: debug-connection
skill.description: Debug WebSocket connection issues between the CLI and FigJam plugin when diagrams do not sync or the connection fails.
skill.summary: Guides CLI and FigJam plugin WebSocket troubleshooting with local diagnostics, protocol checks, and validation steps.
skill.author: 7nohe

security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command examples, and TypeScript protocol snippets in SKILL.md. static_findings.snippet: **Solution**: Start CLI with `bun run packages/cli/src/index.ts serve diagram.yaml`
**Check**: Ensure `--secret` flag value matches between CLI and plugin

content.value_statement: FigJam diagram syncing can fail when the CLI, plugin UI, or plugin main thread loses WebSocket state. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through local checks, protocol review, and validation steps.
actual_capabilities: Maps the CLI, plugin UI, and plugin main thread connection path.
Lists symptoms and checks for refused, dropped, or unauthenticated WebSocket connections.
Explains where to inspect CLI output, browser console events, network frames, and Figma console errors.
Documents expected hello, full sync, patch, and error message flow.
Suggests local diagnostic commands for port checks, serve mode, authentication, and YAML validation.
limitations: Does not modify plugin or CLI source code automatically.
Assumes the FigJam plugin and figram CLI project are already available locally.
Diagnostic commands may differ by operating system and installed tools.
Does not validate remote WebSocket services or production deployments.

use_cases.title: Restore Local Sync
use_cases.description: Diagnose why a local FigJam plugin connects but stops updating the canvas.

use_cases.title: Verify CLI Setup
use_cases.description: Check serve mode, ports, secrets, and YAML validation before testing plugin rendering.

use_cases.title: Support Team Triage
use_cases.description: Collect reproducible connection symptoms and console checks from users without changing project code.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Connection Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debug-connection skill to help me find why my FigJam plugin stays on Connecting. Ask for only the needed local details first.

prompt_templates.title: Sync Drop Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose a connection that works at first and then stops syncing. Compare CLI logs, plugin UI console events, and YAML parse errors.

prompt_templates.title: Protocol Message Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my WebSocket message flow. Check whether hello, full sync, patch, request full, and error messages are in the expected order.

prompt_templates.title: Authenticated Port Debug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a step-by-step diagnostic plan for a custom port and shared secret setup. Include checks for CLI serve mode, plugin settings, and validation failures.

output_examples.input: My plugin says Connecting forever after I start the FigJam plugin.
output: Check that the CLI serve process is running for the same diagram file.
Confirm the plugin is using the expected local WebSocket port.
Inspect the plugin UI console for connection errors before changing code.

output_examples.input: The canvas updates once, then stops after I edit YAML.
output_examples.output: Likely causes include YAML validation failures, patch generation errors, or plugin main rendering errors. Compare the CLI terminal and both plugin consoles.

output_examples.input: Authentication closes the connection after connect.
output: Verify that the CLI and plugin use the same temporary secret value.
Redact real secrets from logs before sharing them.
Review the connection hello step and server rejection message.

best_practices: Confirm the CLI server is running before inspecting plugin-side errors.
Compare the plugin UI console, Figma console, and CLI terminal for the same timestamp.
Use a temporary test diagram before debugging a complex production diagram.
anti_patterns: Changing plugin code before confirming the WebSocket server, port, and secret.
Ignoring YAML validation errors while troubleshooting sync failures.
Sharing real authentication secrets or private diagram content in troubleshooting prompts.

faq.question: Can this skill run diagnostics for me?
faq.answer: It can guide local diagnostic commands, but the user or agent environment must execute them with appropriate permission.

faq.question: Does it require a live FigJam file?
faq.answer: No. A local test diagram is usually enough to check the WebSocket connection and message flow.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it fix YAML syntax errors?
faq.answer: It helps identify YAML validation problems and points to the failing stage, but it does not rewrite files automatically.

faq.question: Can it debug custom ports?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for custom WebSocket ports and matching plugin settings.

faq.question: Is it safe for production secrets?
faq.answer: No. Use temporary test secrets and redact sensitive values before sharing logs or prompts.
